messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values? Wait facilities param type: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That seems ambiguous: It might accept a single facility or an array? The description says "Facilities and sections in public library." So maybe we pass an array of strings? But the type says union of string literal types or array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe". But the other options are singular. Might be a mistake. We'll assume we can pass an array of strings specifying required facilities.

We need to find libraries in New York with Reading Room and Fiction. Then in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and Children Section. Then in Chicago with Cafe and Reading Room.

We'll call function thrice. Use location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room","Fiction"]. Next: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi","Children Section"]. Next: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe","Reading Room"].

Return results.
